description: Canonical controlled vocabulary for classifying evidence used by A.R.I.A. Evidence is case-specific information that may support, contradict, discriminate between, validate, invalidate, or otherwise materially affect technical reasoning. This Registry defines evidence classification and handling semantics; it does not define source authority, confidence, probability, case state, or the persisted evidence object schema.

principles: Evidence records what was observed, measured, reported, retrieved, captured, tested, calculated, or otherwise established for a technical case.
Evidence remains distinct from interpretation, inference, hypothesis, diagnosis, and canonical knowledge.
Evidence shall preserve provenance sufficient to determine where it came from and how it was obtained.
Evidence type classifies the nature of the evidence; it does not assign source authority or diagnostic truth.
The same evidence item may support one hypothesis while contradicting another.
Evidence may be incomplete, ambiguous, stale, superseded, contradicted, or invalid without being deleted from historical record.
Evidence shall reference canonical entities rather than recreate them.
Measurements represented by evidence retain canonical measurement identity and units.
Evidence applicability may depend on technical context.
Evidence freshness may materially affect diagnostic value.
Evidence strength is contextual and shall not be inferred solely from evidence type.
Direct observation does not automatically establish cause.
A test result establishes what the test demonstrated within its conditions; it does not automatically establish universal causal truth.
Historical experience may inform reasoning but is not equivalent to current-case evidence unless represented through an appropriate current-case evidence record.
A.R.I.A.-generated interpretation shall not become self-validating evidence merely because A.R.I.A. produced it.

categories.description: Directly observed technical or physical conditions.
Measured technical quantities or instrument-derived readings.
Technical state, telemetry, alarms, counters, events, or logs produced by equipment or software systems.
Observed, retrieved, exported, or recorded configuration information.
Photographic, screenshot, video, or other visual technical evidence.
Technical information supplied by a person.
Technical information contained in documents, standards, designs, records, procedures, or other documentary sources.
Evidence produced through deliberate technical testing or validation.
Environmental information materially relevant to technical behavior.
Evidence deterministically or structurally derived from other evidence or known inputs.
Observed technical result following a deliberate technical change or corrective action.
Relevant technical evidence that cannot yet be classified into another controlled evidence category.

evidence_types.description: A technical condition, behavior, symptom, event, or other relevant fact directly reported by the user.
rules: The report establishes what the user reported, not necessarily that the reported interpretation is technically correct.
Observation and interpretation should remain distinguishable when both are supplied.

evidence_types.description: A technical or physical condition directly observed and reported by a technician.
rules: The observed condition should be separated from any causal conclusion supplied by the technician.

evidence_types.description: A technical condition, design condition, system behavior, or other relevant fact directly observed and reported by an engineer.
Evidence produced through direct physical inspection of equipment, cabling, antennas, connectors, structures, installation, components, or other technical conditions.
A technical quantity measured directly using equipment, an instrument, a tester, or another defined measurement method.
rules: The underlying measurement shall retain measurement identity, value, unit, method, time, and provenance when applicable.
Measurement quality depends on method, instrument, conditions, calibration where relevant, and applicability.

evidence_types.description: A technical value or state reported directly by equipment, embedded software, controller, management platform, or another technical system.
rules: A system reading establishes what the system reported at the applicable time.
System reporting accuracy may require independent validation when technically material.

evidence_types.description: A current or historical alarm, fault indication, warning, or equivalent condition generated by equipment or a technical system.
rules: An alarm establishes that the originating system reported the alarm condition.
An alarm does not independently establish root cause.

evidence_types.description: A counter, statistic, KPI, performance metric, error count, utilization value, or similar technical metric reported by a system.
Timestamped technical information contained in equipment, operating-system, application, controller, network, management-system, or other system logs.
rules: Log timestamps and originating system shall be preserved when available.
A log message may describe a detected condition without establishing its underlying cause.

evidence_types.description: A recorded technical event, state transition, restart, failover, synchronization event, link event, configuration event, or equivalent system occurrence.
Configuration retrieved from the currently applicable equipment or authoritative management system.
rules: Retrieval time shall be retained when configuration may change.
Live configuration establishes observed configuration state, not necessarily intended configuration.

evidence_types.description: A configuration file, backup, export, structured dataset, or equivalent configuration artifact.
rules: The configuration's originating system, applicable equipment, and effective or capture time should be preserved when known.

evidence_types.description: A specific configuration parameter or setting represented as evidence.
A screenshot containing technically relevant state, configuration, measurement, alarm, log, performance, topology, or other information.
rules: The screenshot is evidence of what was displayed when captured.
Relevant displayed values may be extracted into structured evidence while retaining linkage to the screenshot source.

evidence_types.description: A photograph containing technically relevant physical, installation, equipment, component, path, environmental, or other field information.
rules: A photograph establishes only conditions visible or defensibly inferable from the image.
Image interpretation shall remain distinguishable from the underlying photograph.

evidence_types.description: A video recording containing technically relevant physical, operational, equipment, installation, environmental, or temporal information.
A technical statement supplied by a person that does not fit a more specific observation type.
rules: The identity or role of the speaker shall not by itself determine truth.
Statements based on recollection should remain distinguishable from direct current observation.

evidence_types.description: Technical information supplied from memory rather than from a directly available current observation or artifact.
rules: Recollection may be useful but should preserve uncertainty and should not be silently upgraded to direct observation.

evidence_types.description: Technical information formally published, issued, or supplied by the applicable manufacturer.
rules: Manufacturer identity, product applicability, variant applicability, revision applicability, and publication validity shall be considered separately.
Manufacturer documentation may be authoritative for intended product behavior without proving the current physical state of a specific installation.

evidence_types.description: Manufacturer-issued release notes, defect notices, compatibility information, software changes, firmware changes, or equivalent product-change documentation.
An approved or otherwise applicable engineering design, path design, RF design, configuration design, drawing, calculation package, or technical design artifact.
rules: A design establishes intended or engineered state, not necessarily current installed state.

evidence_types.description: An applicable technical standard, requirement, specification, procedure, safety requirement, regulatory requirement, or industry standard.
rules: Applicability, revision, issuing authority, and effective period shall be considered when technically material.

evidence_types.description: A documented technical installation, commissioning, maintenance, troubleshooting, test, validation, or corrective procedure.
Recorded commissioning measurements, configuration, acceptance results, test results, or related technical closeout information.
rules: Commissioning records establish recorded historical state and shall not automatically be treated as current state.

evidence_types.description: Documentation representing the installed physical, logical, configuration, or topology state of a completed system.
rules: An as-built record may become stale after later modifications.

evidence_types.description: A technical record of maintenance, repair, replacement, inspection, adjustment, upgrade, or other intervention.
Evidence produced by a deliberate diagnostic test intended to evaluate a technical condition or hypothesis.
rules: Test method, conditions, inputs, expected result, actual result, and applicable context should be retained when material.
A test result shall be interpreted only within the discriminatory capability of the test.

evidence_types.description: Evidence produced by a controlled test intended to isolate a component, path, configuration, interface, endpoint, environmental factor, or other technical variable.
rules: Isolation evidence may strongly discriminate between hypotheses when the changed variable and test conditions are controlled.
Uncontrolled simultaneous changes reduce discriminatory value.

evidence_types.description: Evidence produced by comparing technically relevant systems, sides, components, paths, configurations, periods, or other controlled comparison targets.
Evidence produced by testing whether a system, component, configuration, repair, installation, or corrective action satisfies defined technical acceptance criteria.
rules: Validation success establishes satisfaction of the tested criteria under the validation conditions.
Validation success does not automatically prove that a proposed root cause was correct.

evidence_types.description: Structured evidence comparing technically relevant conditions before and after a deliberate action or change.
rules: Before and after evidence has greatest causal value when other material variables are controlled.
Improvement after a change does not automatically prove exclusivity of cause.

evidence_types.description: Observed or measured technical outcome following a corrective action.
rules: Action completion and successful correction are distinct.
Successful recovery may support a causal hypothesis but does not automatically prove it.
The action itself belongs to the action model; this evidence type records the resulting technical outcome.

evidence_types.description: Observed or reported environmental information materially relevant to technical behavior.
Measured environmental quantity materially relevant to technical behavior, such as temperature, wind, precipitation, humidity, icing, or other environmental conditions.
rules: Measured environmental quantities shall retain measurement identity and units when represented as measurements.

evidence_types.description: A reproducible technical value or result derived through a defined deterministic calculation from known inputs.
rules: The calculation method and input evidence or measurements shall remain traceable.
A deterministic calculation does not gain more authority than its method and inputs support.

evidence_types.description: A structured technical pattern derived from multiple current-case evidence items.
rules: The pattern shall retain links to the evidence from which it was derived.
A derived pattern is evidence about the relationship among observations; causal interpretation remains separate.

evidence_types.description: Relevant technical evidence that cannot yet be classified confidently as another controlled evidence type.
rules: OTHER should be used only when no existing evidence type adequately represents the information.
Repeated use of OTHER for the same evidence class should trigger Registry review rather than uncontrolled vocabulary growth.

classification_rules.rule: Evidence type shall describe the nature of the evidence, not whether A.R.I.A. agrees with it.
Evidence type shall not encode confidence, reliability, probability, source authority, or hypothesis disposition.
The most specific applicable evidence type should be used.
Evidence shall not be reclassified merely because later reasoning changes its diagnostic significance.
An artifact may generate multiple structured evidence records when it independently establishes multiple technically meaningful observations.
Multiple evidence records derived from one artifact shall preserve shared provenance to that artifact.
A screenshot containing a displayed measurement may remain SCREENSHOT evidence while the extracted value is represented separately as measurement evidence when useful.
A photograph containing a visible physical defect may remain PHOTOGRAPH evidence while the structured observed condition is represented separately as PHYSICAL_INSPECTION evidence when useful.
A document is not automatically current-case evidence merely because it exists; its technical relevance and applicability to the current case must be established.

Historical frequency, prior cases, manufacturer history, product history, user history, and team history belong primarily to the Experience Ledger and prior reasoning rather than being treated as ordinary current-case evidence types.
Canonical Knowledge Graph relationships are not ordinary evidence types. Evidence may support or challenge canonical knowledge, but knowledge and evidence remain distinct.
A.R.I.A. inference is not a standalone evidence type. Inference must remain traceable to the evidence, knowledge, experience, and reasoning operation from which it was produced.
Interpretation shall not silently overwrite the underlying observation.
Evidence that becomes superseded, contradicted, invalidated, or retracted shall remain historically traceable.
Unknown evidence classification shall use OTHER rather than creating uncontrolled evidence-type strings.

provenance_semantics.principle: Every material evidence record must preserve enough provenance to determine what produced the evidence and how the evidence entered A.R.I.A.
rules: Evidence provenance shall identify the originating person, system, source, artifact, instrument, test, action, or derivation when applicable.
Evidence derived from another evidence item shall retain lineage to the parent evidence.
Evidence extracted from an artifact shall retain linkage to the artifact.
A transformed or normalized representation shall not erase the original evidence.
Provenance does not by itself establish source authority.

freshness_semantics.principle: Evidence freshness is evidence-specific and context-specific.
rules: Evidence marked freshness_sensitive requires temporal applicability to be considered when materially affecting reasoning.
Historical evidence is not invalid merely because it is old.
A current-state question should prefer sufficiently current evidence over stale evidence when both describe the same technical condition.
A historical-state question may require evidence from the historical period rather than the newest available evidence.
Configuration, software, firmware, topology, alarms, performance, environmental conditions, and live system state are commonly freshness-sensitive.
Document revision and effective date may be more important than retrieval date.

applicability_semantics.principle: Evidence may only influence reasoning to the extent that it applies to the technical object, condition, time, configuration, and question being evaluated.
rules: Applicability may depend on manufacturer, product family, product, variant, revision, software, firmware, configuration, topology, scope, site, environment, procedure, or time.
Context applicability should use the authoritative context model defined by Core/Registries/context_types.json and Core/Schemas/context.schema.json.
A technically authoritative source may still provide inapplicable evidence for a different product, version, configuration, or time.
Applicability and source authority shall remain separate.

diagnostic_semantics.principle: Evidence changes the defensibility of technical hypotheses through explicit reasoning; evidence type alone does not determine the amount or direction of that change.

roles.description: The evidence increases support for a hypothesis.
The evidence decreases support for a hypothesis.
The evidence materially distinguishes between competing hypotheses.
The evidence satisfies defined confirmation criteria for a hypothesis or technical conclusion.
The evidence satisfies defined criteria for eliminating a hypothesis.
The evidence establishes that defined technical acceptance criteria were satisfied.
The evidence materially informs context without directly supporting or contradicting a specific hypothesis.
The evidence is relevant to the case but currently has no material directional effect on the evaluated hypothesis.

rules: Diagnostic role is relationship-specific and shall not be treated as an immutable property of the evidence item.
The same evidence item may have different diagnostic roles relative to different hypotheses.
CONFIRMATORY and ELIMINATING roles require defined reasoning criteria; they are not assigned solely because evidence appears strong.
Validation of technical recovery is distinct from confirmation of root cause.
Contradictory evidence shall not be discarded merely because it conflicts with the leading hypothesis.

derived_evidence_semantics.principle: Derived evidence may summarize or calculate relationships among evidence without becoming independent corroboration of its own inputs.
rules: Derived evidence shall retain lineage to all materially contributing evidence or measurements.
A.R.I.A. shall not count an observation and a deterministic transformation of that same observation as two independent corroborating sources.
Derived patterns shall not become self-validating causal conclusions.
Model-generated reasoning is not evidence merely because it references evidence.
If model output identifies a new observable claim, that claim requires independent observation, retrieval, measurement, or validation before being treated as established evidence.

historical_learning_boundary.principle: Current-case evidence, historical experience, and canonical knowledge are separate memory classes.
rules: Prior cases are stored and evaluated through the Experience Ledger rather than represented as a generic PRIOR_CASE evidence type.
Aggregated case patterns inform empirical priors and learned expectations rather than masquerading as direct current-case observations.
Manufacturer history, product history, configuration history, user history, and team history require context matching before influencing current reasoning.
Historical frequency shall not independently establish current-case cause.
A validated historical case may inform a hypothesis prior without being inserted into the current case as duplicate evidence.
Knowledge Graph facts may guide interpretation and test selection but remain distinct from current-case evidence.

source_authority_boundary.principle: Evidence classification and source authority are independent.
rules: This Registry shall not assign HIGH, MEDIUM, LOW, VERY_HIGH, MODERATE, or similar reliability labels to evidence types.
Source authority shall be evaluated using the applicable source and provenance contracts.
A technician observation is not inherently less reliable than an engineer observation.
A manufacturer document may be authoritative for intended behavior while being irrelevant to the current installed condition.
A system-generated value may be precise but still incorrect if the underlying sensor, configuration, clock, or reporting mechanism is faulty.
Corroboration, method quality, applicability, freshness, and provenance may affect evidentiary confidence independently of evidence type.

confidence_boundary.principle: Evidence type does not own confidence.
rules: Evidence confidence shall use the shared confidence contract established by Core/Schemas/core_contracts.json.
Evidence confidence shall not be encoded as an evidence type.
Context-match confidence shall remain separate from evidence confidence.
Source authority shall remain separate from evidence confidence.
Hypothesis probability shall remain separate from evidence confidence.
Confidence in an interpretation shall not silently transfer to the underlying evidence or vice versa.

prohibited_uses: Assigning a universal reliability score based only on evidence type.
Treating evidence type as source authority.
Treating evidence type as hypothesis probability.
Treating an alarm as automatic proof of root cause.
Treating a design as proof of current installed state.
Treating an as-built record as automatically current.
Treating successful recovery as automatic proof of causal diagnosis.
Treating an A.R.I.A. inference as self-validating evidence.
Treating historical frequency as direct current-case evidence.
Treating Knowledge Graph relationships as current-case observations.
Duplicating canonical manufacturers, products, variants, symptoms, failure modes, measurements, units, or context objects inside evidence records.
Discarding contradictory evidence because it conflicts with the current leading hypothesis.
Counting derived evidence as independent corroboration of its own parent evidence.
Silently replacing an observation with an interpretation.
Deleting invalidated or superseded evidence when historical traceability is required.
Using evidence vocabulary to define case reasoning state or lifecycle status.
Using evidence records as a substitute for the Experience Ledger.
Using evidence records as a substitute for the Knowledge Graph.
